answer: A stake-bonded reputation graph makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent identity must lock a deposit before it can transact, and its past work is scored at a single reputation vertex in the network. Good work raises the score and opens a haven of trusted counterparties, while cheating slashes the deposit and stains that vertex. An attacker must fund each fake identity separately, so forging a thousand umber-shadowed sock puppets costs a thousand deposits, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its standing.
